guarantees.claim: When err_processed_i is high, cfg_entropy_ready is cleared to 0 on the next clock edge, taking priority over any set condition.
When not in reset, err_processed_i is low, entropy_ready_pulse_i is high, and st equals StIdle, cfg_entropy_ready is set to 1.
During active-low reset, cfg_entropy_ready is cleared to 0.
When no active condition (reset, err_processed_i, or set) is true, cfg_entropy_ready retains its previous value.

assumptions.claim: The state signal st must be a valid, stable FSM state and StIdle must be a defined encoding; undefined or metastable st could cause incorrect setting or retention of cfg_entropy_ready.
assumptions.risk: cfg_entropy_ready may be set when not intended or fail to set when expected, leading to entropy flow mismanagement.

assumptions.claim: err_processed_i must be synchronously asserted/deasserted and not glitch; a glitch could spuriously clear cfg_entropy_ready.
assumptions.risk: Loss of the entropy-ready indicator, potentially stalling downstream consumers.

uncertain_points.claim: If entropy_ready_pulse_i asserts while st != StIdle, the pulse is ignored and cfg_entropy_ready remains low. It is unclear whether this can cause a missed entropy-ready event.
uncertain_points.risk: Entropy availability may be missed, requiring a re-arming or stalling the system indefinitely.

uncertain_points.claim: When err_processed_i and entropy_ready_pulse_i coincide (with st == StIdle), err_processed_i clears cfg_entropy_ready, discarding the entropy-ready event. It is unknown whether this priority is safe for entropy integrity.
uncertain_points.risk: Loss of an entropy-ready notification during error processing may compromise randomness availability or cause a security impact.

uncertain_points.claim: The FSM generating st is external; without its definition it is unclear whether StIdle is the only state where entropy ready should be latched. Another state might also require capture.
uncertain_points.risk: Incomplete entropy ready handling across all FSM states.
